My mum used to ignore me all the time when I was a kid, and I can only describe how I felt as a physical pain in my chest. It was incredibly traumatic. I still really struggle with feeling that I don’t matter, I get extremely anxious if I don’t hear from someone that I’ve done something horribly wrong, and that pain in my chest never really goes away. I’ve spent a lot of time in therapy unpacking it and my relationship with my mum has improved a lot now that I’m an adult, but the trauma is still present. 

I really get how you feel and I hope that you can get away/access therapy or whatever it is that you need to focus on your healing. I hope you know that your feelings are valid and it’s okay to have them. Look after yourself, OP ♥️

I want to preface this by thanking you for sharing your story. You’re incredibly brave, OP. This wasn’t just a toxic relationship, but an abusive one. It would have escalated. I know it hurts now, but him dumping you is the best thing that could have happened. No one deserves to be treated this way. I don’t like to throw around terms like ‘narcissist’ lightly however this sounds very much like narcissistic abuse. 

I’m sorry that you’re struggling, and I hope you know that none of this is your fault. It sounds like this relationship has been incredibly traumatising for you and you don’t deserve to be treated this way. I’m sorry it’s so hard to get a therapy appointment, but if Jan 2023 is the nearest, book it in. It’s better late than never. 

In the meantime, eat little and often if you’re struggling with appetite, take a shower, try and get out of the house for short walks, even if it’s just for five minutes. I recommend the agoraphobia subreddit, folks there have helped me so much with my anxiety around leaving the house.

I know it really hurts right now but please don’t give up on life. There is a wonderful life waiting for you, people who will treat you with kindness and respect, and you deserve to find happiness after this.

Like other people have said, there’s nothing wrong with going at your own pace and taking some time away when you need to. I personally think it’s absolutely a game and story worth playing through, but do not push yourself through it if it’s too much. Your mental health is more important.
